LESSON: BIBLE TRANSLATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Bible 3.2 Divisions of the Bible (6 lessons) By the end of the sub- strand, 
Topic 3.3: Bible Translation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Bible Translation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to translate the Bible into different languages?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify versions of the Bible used today
2. discuss reasons for translating the Bible into local languages
3. describe the translation of the Bible from the original languages to local languages
4. appreciate the work of Bible translation in Kenya

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: BIBLE TRANSLATION
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Bible Translation helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: BIBLE TRANSLATION
Study Bible Translation like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify versions of the Bible used today

What this means
In this part you learn to identify versions of the Bible used today. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify versions of the Bible used today.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Bible Translation” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify versions of the Bible used today. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Discuss reasons for translating the Bible into local languages

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss reasons for translating the Bible into local languages. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss reasons for translating the Bible into local languages.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Bible Translation in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss reasons for translating the Bible into local languages. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe the translation of the Bible from the original languages to local languages

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the translation of the Bible from the original languages to local languages. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the translation of the Bible from the original languages to local languages.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the translation of the Bible from the original languages to local languages. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the work of Bible translation in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the work of Bible translation in Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the work of Bible translation in Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Bible Translation” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the work of Bible translation in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Bible Translation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Bible Translation” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify versions of the Bible used today)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Bible Translation in your own words. (skill: discuss reasons for translating the Bible into local languages)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: describe the translation of the Bible from the original languages to local languages)

Example 4: Show how “Bible Translation” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: appreciate the work of Bible translation in Kenya)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Bible Translation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify versions of the Bible used today.
3. Practise this skill: discuss reasons for translating the Bible into local languages.
4. Practise this skill: describe the translation of the Bible from the original languages to local languages.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Bible Translation from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Bible Translation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Bible Translation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to translate the Bible into different languages?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Bible Translation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify versions of the Bible used today.
5. Be able to: discuss reasons for translating the Bible into local languages.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
